_preregistration.rung: model ordering must agree across two seeds at fixed construction, else the construction question is undefined
_preregistration.primary: mean pairwise Spearman between the model-rankings different constructions give

verdict: RUNG (seed stability at FIXED construction, checked before the construction question): branching=0.75, s_near=0.9062, s_far=0.8125, distinct=0.7073, top1=0.9722. 5 of 5 readouts rank the models consistently across two seeds at threshold 0.6 -- ['branching', 's_near', 's_far', 'distinct', 'top1']. Only these are asked the primary question; a readout that cannot rank models reproducibly at fixed construction cannot be asked about invariance across them. PRIMARY, mean pairwise agreement between the model-rankings different constructions produce: branching=-0.050, s_near=+0.000, s_far=-0.037, distinct=-0.028, top1=+0.111 over 18 constructions. NONE reaches the registered 0.6 threshold. No readout ranks models consistently across constructions, so on this evidence the instrument characterises LATTICES rather than language models, and any single-construction comparison is a fact about the apparatus. CONSTRUCTION-DOMINATED at or below 0.3: ['branching', 's_near', 's_far', 'distinct', 'top1']. BOUNDARY: 3 models, so each ranking has 3 points and one swap moves rho a long way -- this identifies a SCRAMBLED readout far more confidently than it certifies an invariant one. One temperature (T=0.7), one lattice size (N=48), radii [2, 3]. Constructions are RULES applied to each model's own tokenizer and marginal, not shared token ids, since identical ids across different vocabularies would not be comparable.
